transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Peregrine Head of Product), Liam O'Connor (Peregrine ML Eng), Rajiv Malhotra (Peregrine CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Peregrine is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for rapid internal features, and a private VPC for regulated customer data. Key concerns: context window (some use-cases need 8k-64k), multilingual support (EN+JP+ES), tool-calling to orchestration systems, and security/SOC2/KMS. They want a benchmark with their prompt families and estimate cost tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private. Redwood to send pricing and run a benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll hand over to Diego for the deep bit but quickly, we're Maya, AE, and Diego is our solutions eng. Could we do quick intros on the Peregrine side?
[00:16] Asha (Peregrine Head of Product): Sure, I'm Asha, I run product. We own the conversational agent for Peregrine’s support stack. Liam is the ML eng who actually runs the models and Rajiv is our CTO.
[00:26] Liam (Peregrine ML Eng): Hey all. Quick context, we've been prototyping with open-source models — Mixtral / Llama-derived — and also testing Anthropic for safety. Our main ask: 1) long context for multi-document threads (12–20k tokens typical), 2) tool calling to call our triage system and run DB lookups, 3) good multi-lingual quality for EN/JP/ES.
[00:44] Rajiv (Peregrine CTO): And security: we need SOC2 plus customer-managed keys and audit logs. Plus, low variance in latency — peak 95th < 350ms for small responses.
[00:57] Diego (Redwood SE): Got it. That aligns with what we've seen. A couple of immediate clarifying q's: when you say 12–20k tokens, is that active context (KV cache live) for every request, or just longer initial docs? And what's the percent of requests that truly use full context?
[01:15] Liam: Hmm, probably about 15% of requests are the big ones with full thread (12–20k) but they drive correctness. The rest are short. We also do batch offline embeddings for search.
[01:27] Maya: Good to know. Diego, can you run through Redwood's model catalog and hosting options quickly — especially open models and quantization profiles?
[01:33] Diego: Yeah. High level: Hosted API gives fastest onboarding and we host a curated set of open models + Redwood-verified performance. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for consistent throughput and stronger data isolation; Private is VPC/on-prem with customer-managed keys and full audit. For models, we support varieties: Llama-3-family variants (many forks), Mistral, Falcon, Mixtral and a few newer efficient families — we also carry quantized variants (8-bit, int4 for cheap throughput). We do kernel selection at runtime, and have KV prefix caching to reduce tokens for repeated context.
[02:02] Asha: Quick Q — you say int4, do you ship those to hosted? Concerned about hallucination quality regressions.
[02:09] Diego: Yes, we expose quantized model variants with measured perf/quality tradeoffs. We usually recommend starting with int8/q4 on critical generation and run quality evals; int4 is good for high-throughput non-critical paths. We'll show a bench.
[02:22] Rajiv: What about context lengths? We have documents up to ~50k tokens in a few cases. Is that realistic?
[02:28] Diego: We currently have production paths up to 64k for certain model families — often with sparse attention variants or chunked retrieval. For very large docs we recommend retrieval + reranking to avoid quadratic cost. But of course if you need full 50–64k KV live, we can route to specific model variants or Dedicated instances tuned for long context.
[02:44] Liam: Are there differences in routing latency for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? If I pin a model to Dedicated, will that actually reduce tail variance?
[02:52] Diego: Yes — Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs, so the queueing variability is lower. Hosted is multitenant but with autoscaling — for most workloads it's fine, but Dedicated wins on 95th-percentile stability. Private (VPC) can be provisioned similarly to Dedicated but adds network egress and onboarding time.
[03:07] Maya: Also a quick note on fallback policy — we can configure fallbacks to smaller models on capacity constraints and route by cost/latency tiers.
[03:13] [Brief crosstalk]
[03:20] Asha: Tool calling: we need to call our triage microservice (sync and async) plus execute signed DB reads. How mature is Redwood's function-calling and structured outputs?
[03:31] Diego: We support function/tool calling with typed schemas and structured JSON outputs. We also do streaming responses and have hooks for your orchestration — webhooks, gRPC, or direct SDK calls. For sensitive DB reads you can keep those in your VPC and only send the minimal prompt to the model; we also support encryption in transit with customer-managed KMS on Private.
[03:51] Rajiv: Any limits on attachments or binary blobs? We sometimes pass small embeddings or base64 pieces.
[03:58] Diego: No hard limit beyond payload size; we recommend embeddings for chunked context instead of full blobs.
[04:05] Liam: On multilingual: we've seen Llama-based and Mistral variants do okay in JP, but we care about domain-specific vocabulary. What's your eval approach?
[04:14] Diego: We do per-language evals using your prompts — Rouge/BLEU-style and semantic evals. Also can run quality monitors and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll want samples from you (prompt families and reference outputs) to baseline.
[04:28] Asha: Perfect. About security, do you have SOC 2 Type II? And can we get a penetration test report?
[04:35] Maya: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the security pack and pen-test summary. Private deployments can integrate with your HSM/KMS.
[04:43] Rajiv: For Private, what's the typical onboarding timeline? We estimated 6–8 weeks.
[04:48] Diego: For VPC-hosted Private with Redwood control plane, typically 4–6 weeks for standard setups. On-prem full air-gapped instances are longer — 8–12 weeks — depends on compliance and your infra.
[04:58] Maya: Also note Dedicated reserved capacity contracts are monthly/annual — can be faster to get you predictable capacity if you want to avoid full Private.
[05:06] Liam: Benchmarks — can you run a throughput test with our sample dataset and a pinned model? We want latency P50 and P95, memory footprint, and token costs.
[05:14] Diego: Absolutely. If you share three prompt families and a sample trace (we asked for 2k token context traces earlier), we can run a 1-hour throughput test across hosted and Dedicated variants and send the csv.
[05:25] [Silence / note-taking]
[05:33] Asha: Pricing: general question — what's the hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved cost model? We want rough numbers so we can model.
[05:41] Maya: We'll send a pricing matrix — hosted is usage-based (per token/embedding), Dedicated is commit-based (monthly or annual reserved GPU pricing plus overage). We'll include example TCOs for int8 and int4 operation.
[05:52] Rajiv: Any mention of competitors — we did a bench vs OpenAI and Anthropic earlier. Curious where Redwood typically fits on latency/cost.
[05:59] Diego: We generally target being competitive with managed endpoints but with more control — you often get better cost per token on Dedicated, and more predictable tail-latency. We'll include comparative notes versus OpenAI/Anthropic and an apples-to-apples on model quality.
[06:12] Maya: Alright, quick recap and next steps: Maya will send security + pricing. Diego will run bench once Peregrine shares traces. Peregrine to share prompt families and access materials. We'll schedule a Private onboarding demo in next week. Anything else?
[06:27] Asha: Could you also include an example of a fallback policy config and canary rollout doc? We need to show to ops.
[06:34] Diego: Yep, we'll include the rollout/how-to doc and examples of routing policy.
[06:39] Rajiv: Ok that sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:43] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
